title: Linear Equations: Lines, Slopes, and Intersections

questions.question: In y = mx + c, what does m represent?
questions.rationale: m is the slope — rise over run. c is the intercept, the y-value when x = 0.

questions.question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 3) and (3, 11).
A line with slope 4 passing through (1, 3) has equation:
questions.rationale: Substitute: 3 = 4(1) + c gives c = −1, so y = 4x − 1.

questions.question: Two distinct lines are parallel exactly when:
options: Their slopes are equal but intercepts differ
questions.rationale: Equal slopes mean identical tilt; different intercepts keep them apart forever, so they never meet.

questions.question: Where do y = 2x + 1 and y = x + 5 intersect?
questions.rationale: Set equal: 2x + 1 = x + 5 → x = 4; then y = 2(4)+1 = 9. Intersection at (4, 9).

questions.question: What is the slope of any horizontal line?
questions.rationale: Horizontal lines never rise, rise/run = 0/distance = 0; their equation is just y = c.

questions.question: If two lines are perpendicular and one has slope 2, the other has slope:
questions.rationale: Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, so the partner of 2 is −1/2 (the negative reciprocal).

questions.question: The midpoint of the segment joining (2, 3) and (6, 11) is:
In a cost–revenue chart, the break-even point corresponds to:
options: Where the cost line crosses the revenue line
The steepest point of either line
questions.rationale: Break-even is where cost equals revenue — the intersection of the two linear graphs.
